Projects are integral to Algorithmic Economics. They convert passive understanding into reproducible research skills.

## Project progression

### [Data Labs](data-labs.qmd)
Short exercises using real or simulated data to implement concepts and algorithms.

### [Replication Projects](replications.qmd)
Structured reproductions of published theoretical, computational, experimental, or empirical results.

### [Capstone Projects](capstones.qmd)
Larger projects combining an economic question, formal model, computational implementation, evidence, evaluation, and a research extension.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Common project architecture

1. Define the economic or institutional problem.
2. Specify agents, preferences, information, actions, and constraints.
3. Formulate the computational problem.
4. Implement the algorithm or model.
5. Use real data, synthetic data, or an appropriate simulation environment.
6. Compare against a benchmark.
7. Reproduce or validate an existing result where possible.
8. Conduct sensitivity and robustness analysis.
9. Identify strategic, computational, empirical, or governance limitations.
10. Propose an extension.
:::
